A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiniteYou work. All 11 pages, including equations, six figures, two tables and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Table 2, and a user study with 16 participants evaluating 70 sample sets.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative comparisons, ablations, qualitative generation results and user study reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same InfuseNet architecture, residual identity injection, conditional flow-matching objective, and two-stage training with synthetic SPMS data. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same nine public training datasets plus internal portrait data, synthetic SPMS data, and portrait evaluation benchmark. Figure 6 retains the same control, stylization and object-personalization scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 retain the same evaluated baselines: InstantX's FLUX.1-dev IP-Adapter and PuLID-FLUX. The SDXL comparison in Figure 2 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Training settings, preprocessing and metrics remain unchanged. Both versions evaluate 15 identities with 200 gender-matched prompts, yielding 1,497 outputs, and retain the user study with 16 participants and 70 sample sets.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 retain the same ablations: removing multi-stage training, replacing SPMS with SPSS synthetic data, and adding IPA for identity injection. The qualitative comparisons and plug-and-play demonstrations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate and user-preference reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–2 is unchanged, including InfU's 0.209 ID Loss, 0.318 CLIPScore and 0.221 PickScore. The 72.8% versus 27.2% user preference, qualitative examples and reported findings are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the flow-matching derivation, rectified-flow formulation and InfuseNet block correspondence remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, definition or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning identity preservation, text-image alignment, generation quality, multi-stage training and plug-and-play compatibility.

C2.justification: The explanations of residual identity injection, SPMS training and ablation tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning identity similarity, image quality and potential fake-media synthesis.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains identical implementation details, including eight identity tokens, multiplication factor i = 4, H100 hardware, optimizer settings and training budgets. Project and code/model access information is unchanged; the rewrapped projection-network passage adds no detail.

R1.justification: The same 60 references and research positioning are retained, including the relationships to U-Net methods, PuLID-FLUX, IP-Adapter and ControlNet. No cited work or novelty argument changes.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'dentity-preserved' to 'identity-preserved' in Section 2 and 'th best identity similarity' to 'the best identity similarity' in Section 4.2. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; section organization and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There is localized line reflow in the projection-network passage of Section 4.1 and an updated first-page version/date stamp. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–2 retain the same content, captions, design and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 provides slight editorial polish through two typo corrections and localized text reflow. The methods, empirical evidence, analyses, reproducibility information and limitations are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
